1650:
(a) The final plat shall be clearly and legibly drawn in black ink on suitable permanent reproducible material. The scale of the final plat shall be 100 feet to one-inch or larger. Sheet size shall be 18 inches by 24 inches.
(b) The final plat shall be based on a certified boundary survey delimiting the entirety of the property contained within the final plat, and tied to a city-established monument with the same degree of accuracy as the boundary itself. The survey shall have an accuracy of no less than one in 10,000, and shall meet all requirements of state law regarding the recording of maps and plats.
(c) The final plat shall conform to the approved concept plat and preliminary plat and it may constitute only a portion of the approved concept plat, which the subdivider proposes to record at any one time, provided that such portion conforms to the requirements of these regulations, and said portion is not inconsistent with the public health, safety, or welfare. Any substantial deviation from the approved concept plat or preliminary plat shall require revision and reapproval of both the concept plat and preliminary plat. The final plat shall contain the following information:
(1) Name of the subdivision and unit or phase number, if any.
(2) Names, addresses, and telephone numbers of the property owner of record and the developer or subdivider.
(3) Name, address, and telephone number for each professional firm associated with the portion of the subdivision depicted on the final plat.
(4) Date of plat and survey, north point and graphic scale.
(5) Subdivision location including land lot and land district, area in acres, internal and abutting zoning, proposed number of lots and area represented in tabular format showing associated square footage.
(6) A location sketch or vicinity map positioning the subdivision in relation to the surrounding area with regard to recognized permanent landmarks. The location sketch scale shall be drawn at a scale of 600 feet to one-inch.
(7) Field-run boundary survey of the subdivision property perimeter showing actual bearings in degrees, minutes and seconds and distances in feet and hundredths of a foot along all lines and the bearing and distances to an existing street intersection or other recognized permanent landmark. The boundary information shall be tied and related to the state plane coordinates system, 1983 North American datum, Georgia, west zone.
(8) Municipal or county jurisdictional lines tied to the lines of the subdivision by distance and angles when such lines traverse or adjoin the subdivision; land lot or land district lines traversing or adjoining the subdivision shall also be indicated.
(9) Locations, widths, and names of all streets within and immediately adjoining the plat and all other public or utilities easements or rights-of-way.
(10) Street centerlines showing angles of deflection and standard curve data including radii, chord lengths, and bearings, lengths of arcs and tangents, and points of curvature and tangency.
(11) Lot lines with complete dimensions to the nearest 1/100 of a foot and bearings to the nearest second, and radii, arc and chord lengths, and chord bearings of rounded corners.
(12) Building setback lines with dimensions. When lots are located on a curve or when side lot lines are at angles other than 90 degrees, the lot width at the building line shall be shown.
(13) Lots numbered in numerical order, blocks lettered alphabetically, and addresses as established by the city.
(14) Location, material and size of all drainage pipes, location and type of all drainage system appurtenances such as catchbasins, headwalls and inlets, location and extent of detention ponds with 100-year event level noted, the location, material and size of all city water and sewer mains and appurtenances, the location of all fire hydrants, and the location, width and purpose of any easements, including slope easements.
(15) Location of any areas to be reserved, donated, or dedicated to public use with notes stating their purpose and limitations. Location of any areas to be reserved by private deed covenant for common use of all property owners, or dedicated to a homeowner's association.
(16) A statement of private covenants, if any, and if they are brief enough to be put directly on the final plat; otherwise, if covenants are separately recorded, a statement as follows:
"This plat is subject to the covenants set forth in the separate document(s) attached hereto dated _______, _______ which hereby become a part of this plat, and which were recorded on _______."
(17) Accurate location, material, and description of property corner or line monuments or markers. All monuments and markers shall be in place prior to approval of the final plat.
(18) Extent and elevation of the 100-year floodplain within the subdivision. The origin of the floodplain data shall be indicated. The minimum finished floor elevation (three feet above the 100-year flood elevation) for sites adjacent to the floodplain shall be indicated on the plat for each lot. No part of any lot shall contain a floodplain, state waters buffer, wetlands, or other environmentally protected areas.
(19) Location and boundary of tree save area and/or recompense planting area within the subdivision. No tree save fence shall be removed prior to approval of final plat. Plat shall clearly indicate that no trees shall be removed from a tree save area or recompense planting area. Any lot containing any portion of a tree save area or recompense planting area shall require tree protection plan approval prior to issuance of a site development permit or building permit.
(20) Individual lots, which are deemed by the city engineer as requiring site plans, shall be designated in a readily identifiable manner.
(21) Certificates and statements specified in these regulations.

The steps of the final plat review process are as follows:
(1) Step 1. The developer shall meet with the development coordinator to discuss what is required for final plat approval in terms of documents, fees and schedules.
(2) Step 2. The developer shall submit to the city a complete final plat application package, and that submittal shall be logged in by the administrative assistant. That package must include a landscape plan prepared by a professional landscape architect for all public areas within the subdivision.
(3) Step 3. The final plat application package is carefully checked by the development coordinator to determine whether or not it is complete. If it is incomplete, it needs to be returned to the developer with an explanation of why it is incomplete and what must be done to make it complete. The developer will then begin the process again with step 2 set forth in subsection (2) and no additional fee will be required.
(4) Step 4. If the final plat application package is complete, it will be accepted by the development coordinator; the date of acceptance will be noted; and the final plat will be distributed for staff comments. For every submittal, copies shall be provided to the director of community development, the city engineer, the property manager, the fire marshal and the city's engineering consultant. Copies will also be provided to other staff members on an as-needed basis. The staff shall have at least ten working days for review of the final plat, preparing comments and submitting a report to the development coordinator.
(5) Step 5. After the staff review period, the development coordinator shall schedule a staff review meeting. At least five working days prior to that meeting, all staff members shall be provided a copy of all staff reports.
(6) Step 6. At the staff review meeting, all reports shall be reviewed and all differences resolved. All notes, memos and documents concerning that meeting shall be kept in the project file.
(7) Step 7. The results of the staff meeting shall be combined into a single staff report by the development coordinator. That report shall be reviewed and approved by all participating staff members prior to it being released to the developer.
(8) Step 8. If the staff report concludes the final plat can be placed on a planning and zoning commission agenda, it should be scheduled for the next available regular meeting. If the report concludes the final plat is not acceptable, the final plat shall be returned to the developer with an explanation of why it was found to not be acceptable, and with instructions as to what needs to be done to make it acceptable. The developer will then begin the process again at step 2 set forth in subsection (2) and a new plat review fee will be required.
(9) Step 9. The development coordinator shall forward the approved staff report and the final plat application package to the planning and zoning commission members at least five calendar days prior to the scheduled meeting of the commission. If the report cannot be provided to the members at least five calendar days prior to the meeting, the matter must be rescheduled to a subsequent regular meeting.
(10) Step 10. The planning and zoning commission shall review the final plat and the staff report at the scheduled regular meeting. If the commission approves the final plat, it shall be forwarded to the mayor and council with a recommendation for approval, along with any supplemental conditions or comments. If the commission is not able to approve the final plat, it shall table the matter and provide the developer with instructions as to what needs to be done to secure approval. The developer will then begin the process again with step 2 set forth in subsection (2) and a new plat review fee will be required.
(11) Step 11. The development coordinator shall prepare a staff report for the mayor and council to accompany the package to be forwarded by the planning and zoning commission. The staff report must be reviewed and approved by all staff members involved in the initial staff report and the chairman of the planning and zoning commission. If necessary, a meeting will be held to resolve any differences before the report is submitted to the mayor and council.
(12) Step 12. Following approval of the staff report, it shall be distributed to the mayor and council at least five calendar days prior to a scheduled council meeting. If the report and the final plat application package cannot be distributed at least five calendar days prior to the meeting, the matter will need to be rescheduled to a subsequent regular council meeting.
(13) Step 13. If the developer makes any substantive change to the final plat between the time it is approved by the planning and zoning commission and it is scheduled to be reviewed by the mayor and council, the developer will need to begin the process again with step 2 set forth in subsection (2) and a new plat review fee will be required.
(14) Step 14. The mayor and council shall review the final plat, the staff report, and all related documents and reports at a scheduled regular meeting. If the final plat is approved, the developer will be authorized to proceed with recording the final plat. If approval of the final plat is denied for some reason, the developer shall be provided with the reason for denial and an explanation of what would need to be done to secure approval. In this event, the developer may be required to begin the process again with step 2 set forth in subsection (2) and a new plat review fee will be required. If the mayor and council table the review of the final plat for additional information, the developer shall provide that information to the development coordinator as soon as possible and the developer shall begin the process again with step 11 set forth in subsection (11), but no additional fee shall be required.
(15) Step 15. Prior to recording the final plat, the developer shall provide to the development coordinator a complete and accurate set of as-built drawings in both paper and electronic form. These as-built drawings must be approved by the city engineer and the city's engineering consultant.
(16) Step 16. Prior to recording the final plat, the developer shall complete all required improvements, including the installation of the landscape plan and recompense plantings for the public areas, and those improvements must all be inspected and approved by the city. If for any reason, it is not possible or practical for the developer to be able to complete this work within a reasonable period of time, the developer may post a cash bond, the amount of which shall be determined by the city engineer, pending the satisfactory completion of the work.
(17) Step 17. Prior to recording the final plat, the developer must post with the city an acceptable maintenance bond to guarantee the quality and workmanship of the required improvements as specified in section 77-158(1).
